jobs.description:
"At Klipboard we've introduced a flexible hybrid work policy, where employees spend three days in the office and two days working from home. This approach promotes a balanced work environment that combines office collaboration with the comfort and convenience of remote work."

Klipboard provides specialist software, services and support to deliver fully integrated trading and business management solutions to companies in the distributive trade – wherever they are in the world. With a unique depth of knowledge and experience in ERP/SaaS solutions, Klipboard has a wide range of clients includes wholesalers, distributors, merchants and retailers from small traders to multinational enterprises. Klipboard has offices in the UK, Ireland, The Netherlands, South Africa, Kenya and North America. Our mission is simple: to design and deliver high performance, integrated ERP solutions that enable our distributive trade customers to source effectively, stock efficiently, sell profitably and service competitively.

Klipboard is a global, growing business that embraces AI and emerging technologies to enhance customer outcomes, collaboration, and continuous improvement. We’re looking for people who are curious about or fluid with AI, open to change, and excited to learn how technology can improve the way we work and help our customers which is always supported by strong human insight and communication.

Klipboard’s brand is designed to bring together our expertise across distribution, automotive, retail, rental, transport management, manufacturing, and field service management.

Our passion is to provide customers with an advantage in their incredibly competitive world. We have done this so far by providing flexible, industry specific solutions; software, technology, advice, guidance and expertise built over 40 years of servicing their specific market.

As a Senior E-commerce Implementation Consultant, you will own the successful delivery of e-commerce solutions from discovery and design through configuration, integration, testing, deployment, and adoption. You will work closely with customers to transform their digital commerce capabilities, utilising modern e-commerce platforms, automation technologies, APIs, and AI-driven solutions to improve customer experience, operational efficiency, and revenue growth.

You will act as a trusted advisor to customers, helping them navigate digital transformation initiatives while collaborating with Professional Services, Product, Development, Data & Integration, and Customer Success teams. You will also contribute to the development of Klipboard’s e-commerce consulting capability by mentoring colleagues, creating best practices, and driving innovation through automation and AI.

Key Responsibilities

Lead e-commerce implementation projects from discovery through to go-live, ensuring scope, timeline, quality, and commercial objectives are achieved.
Conduct workshops to understand customer business processes, digital commerce strategies, customer journeys, and operational requirements.
Configure and implement e-commerce platforms and associated integrations with ERP, CRM, payment gateways, shipping providers, marketplaces, and third-party applications.
Design and deliver automation solutions that streamline customer onboarding, product management, order processing, fulfilment workflows, and customer communications.
Apply AI technologies and emerging digital capabilities to improve operational efficiency, customer engagement, personalisation, content generation, analytics, and support processes.
Advise customers on e-commerce best practices, digital transformation opportunities, and scalable commerce architectures.
Collaborate with Data & Integration teams to define and support API, middleware, ETL, and system integration requirements.
Manage project risks, issues, dependencies, and change requests, providing clear communication to customers and internal stakeholders.
Support testing activities, including functional testing, user acceptance testing, data validation, and go-live readiness assessments.
Deliver customer training and knowledge transfer sessions to drive adoption and long-term success.
Act as a subject matter expert for e-commerce consulting and implementation methodologies.
Create and maintain implementation documentation, templates, solution designs, and enablement materials.
Mentor consultants and share knowledge across the Professional Services organisation.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that drive efficiency, repeatability, automation, and scalability across project delivery.

How We Work

Customer-Centric Delivery
You will partner with customers to understand their goals, challenges, and opportunities, ensuring solutions deliver measurable business outcomes.
Innovation Through Technology
You will embrace automation, AI, and modern digital commerce technologies to help customers achieve faster time-to-value and scalable growth.
Collaboration First
You will work closely with Professional Services, Product, Development, Support, Customer Success, and commercial teams to deliver exceptional customer experiences.
Continuous Improvement
You will contribute to the evolution of methodologies, accelerators, automation frameworks, and AI-enabled delivery approaches

Skills, Knowledge And Experience

Proven experience delivering end-to-end e-commerce implementations.
Demonstrable experience with B2B and/or B2C commerce platforms.
Strong understanding of e-commerce business processes, including catalogue management, pricing, promotions, checkout, payment processing, fulfilment, and customer experience.
Experience delivering projects involving ERP, CRM, and third-party system integrations.
Strong knowledge of APIs, integration concepts, and data exchange methodologies.
Experience using automation platforms and workflow technologies such as Power Automate, Zapier, Make, Azure Logic Apps, or equivalent.
Strong understanding of AI technologies and practical applications within e-commerce, customer service, content generation, automation, analytics, and digital transformation.
Excellent customer-facing consultancy and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to facilitate workshops, gather requirements, and translate business needs into solution designs.
Strong problem-solving and analytical capabilities.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
Highly organised with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.
Proficiency in Microsoft 365, including Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint

Nice to have

Experience with modern e-commerce platforms such as Shopify, BigCommerce, Magento/Adobe Commerce, WooCommerce, Shopware, CommerceTools, or similar solutions.
Experience in SaaS, ERP, retail, wholesale distribution, rental, manufacturing, or field service industries.
Experience implementing AI-powered commerce tools and customer experience solutions.
Knowledge of SEO, digital marketing, customer analytics, and conversion optimisation.
Understanding of modern data architectures and customer data platforms.
Experience mentoring consultants and leading project teams.
Familiarity with agile delivery methodologies and project management frameworks.

How you’ll grow and what success looks like (6-12 months)

You are recognised as a trusted advisor for e-commerce, automation, and AI-enabled transformation projects.
You have successfully delivered multiple e-commerce implementations with strong customer outcomes and positive commercial performance.
You are leading customer discussions around automation and AI adoption, helping customers identify opportunities for growth and efficiency.
You have contributed to the development of implementation accelerators, automation frameworks, templates, and best practices used across Professional Services.
You are mentoring consultants and helping build a high-performing e-commerce capability within the organisation.
You are driving innovation in delivery approaches, reducing implementation effort and improving customer time-to-value.

Kerridge Commercial Systems (KCS) is becoming Klipboard and our new brand is designed to bring together our expertise across distribution, automotive, retail, rental, transport management, manufacturing, and field service management. Dewberry is currently seeking a Technical Planning Specialist to join our cadre of skilled professional and technical staff supporting planning, preparedness, mitigation, and operational coordination activities across Alaska, Idaho, Oregon, and Washington.

This position is based in the Seattle/Bothell, Washington area and supports regional planning initiatives focused on natural hazards, operational readiness, and emergency management coordination. Work assignments may include planning efforts associated with Cascadia Subduction Zone earthquake and tsunami scenarios, volcanic hazards within the Cascade Range, continuity planning, logistics planning, and other all hazards preparedness activities.

You will collaborate with emergency management professionals, planners, GIS analysts, and federal, state, local, Tribal, territorial, and private sector stakeholders to develop planning products and analytical solutions that support emergency management decision making.

Dewberry’s Geospatial and Technology Services creates geospatial and analytical solutions for real world engineering, environmental, and community problems. Our analysts provide a variety of data services for our clients including data management, governance, analysis, transformation, automation, and visualization.

Dewberry is a leading, market-facing professional services firm with more than 60 locations and 2,500 professionals nationwide. What sets us apart from our competitors is our people. At Dewberry, we seek out exceptional talent and strive to deliver the highest quality of services to our clients. Whether you’re an experienced professional or a new graduate, you’ll have the chance to collaborate with the best and brightest and work on innovative and complex projects at the forefront of the industry. Responsibilities

Candidates will have strong competencies and demonstrated experience in emergency management planning, stakeholder coordination, and data analysis. Work assignments will include:

Develop, validate, and implement emergency operations plans, hazard mitigation plans, continuity of operations plans, and other planning products.
Apply FEMA’s FOPM Six Step Planning Process to guide planning deliverables and stakeholder engagement.
Support planning task orders through coordination, documentation, technical assistance, and meeting facilitation.
Facilitate stakeholder engagement and interagency coordination for planning efforts.
Assist in the design and execution of exercises to test and improve plans.
Support planning activities related to earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic hazards, continuity, logistics, and regional preparedness initiatives.
Integrate data analysis and geospatial analytics into planning products to support evidence based decision making.
Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis in emergency management policies, programs, and procedures supporting federal agencies.
Develop and implement database management solutions, dashboards, analytical workflows, and data visualization products.
Support GIS based analysis, mapping, and situational awareness activities.
Ensure compliance with applicable government regulations and federal guidance.

Bachelor’s degree in emergency management, public administration, planning, geography, GIS, data science, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in emergency management planning, preferably with FEMA, state emergency management agencies, or other federal deployments.
Familiarity with FEMA’s Incident Command System (ICS), planning doctrine, and disaster operations.
Experience applying the FOPM Six Step Planning Process in real world planning scenarios.
Demonstrated understanding of emergency management planning principles and regional hazard considerations.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Power BI, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 tools, ArcGIS Pro, and ArcGIS Online.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical writing and stakeholder facilitation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in dynamic environments.
Must be eligible to obtain a Public Trust clearance.

Position based in Seattle/Bothell, Washington.
Ability to travel periodically throughout FEMA Region 10 in support of planning activities.
Must have a valid driver’s license, good driving record, and ability to pass a driving record background check.

Description:

ZenPoint Solutions LLC (“ZenPoint Solutions”) is a rapidly expanding Information Technology (IT) services company in the federal sector. We foster a thriving, ambitious work environment that prioritizes employee well-being and a positive company culture. We invite you to join our team and help us shape a dynamic future as we deliver innovative solutions to address the nation's most critical IT missions.

Clearance Requirement:
Active Secret clearance at time of application. Ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret preferred.

Work Location:
Springfield, VA & Washington, D.C.

Work Schedule:
Hybrid work schedule; 3 days onsite, 2 days remote with the ability to change based on customer needs

Position Overview:
ZenPoint Solutions is seeking an IT Strategic Planning Analyst
to join our contractor team supporting a federal client’s enterprise technology program. The analyst produces analysis, draft documentation, and decision-support materials that Government leaders rely on when setting technology direction. The role requires extensive research, analytical rigor, and documentation, including options papers, draft strategy and governance artifacts, investment and cost analyses, roadmap models, and performance reporting. Work products are advisory and are delivered to the Government for review, decision, and adoption. The client retains all decision authority. This role suits an individual who takes real satisfaction in enabling faster, clearer, and better informed decisions. This position reports to the Principal Strategic Advisor & Delivery Lead.

Key Responsibilities:

Research and draft content for the client’s multi-year technology strategy documents and periodic updates, presenting options and supporting analysis for Government review and decision.
Analyze federal IT policy and oversight requirements (FITARA, OMB Circular A-11, and applicable OMB guidance) and prepare plain-language summaries, impact assessments, and draft approaches for Government consideration.
Provide analytic support to Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) processes, including portfolio data analysis, draft business case content, and preparation of draft reporting materials for Government review and submission.
Compile and maintain IT cost transparency and consumption reporting so Government stakeholders can see what enterprise services cost and how usage is trending.
Assemble governance body materials: agendas, read-aheads, briefing decks, draft decision papers, and minutes; maintain the decision and action log at the Government’s direction.
Recommend candidate performance measures and build the reporting that allows Government leaders to track adoption, service health, and delivery progress.
Perform current-state and target-state analysis across the technology portfolio; document gaps and lay out sequencing alternatives with tradeoffs for Government decision.
Apply Government-approved criteria to evaluate incoming requests from component organizations and prepare prioritization and roadmap analysis for Government decision-makers.
Draft charters, standards, operating models, procedures, and policy documentation for Government review and adoption.
Facilitate and document working sessions with Government stakeholders and component representatives; capture outcomes and follow-on actions in concise written products.
Identify and track risks, dependencies, and assumptions; prepare mitigation recommendations for Government consideration.
Produce recurring contract deliverables on the program’s established cadence and in accordance with the deliverable schedule.

Required Qualifications:

Candidate must be a United States Citizen and present proof of Citizenship, if selected
Bachelor’s degree in information technology, business, public administration, or a related field. Additional relevant experience may be substituted for the degree requirement.
Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in IT strategic planning, IT governance, IT portfolio management, or management consulting delivered in support of a federal client.
Demonstrated experience producing executive-level written products – strategy documents, options and decision papers, and briefing materials – delivered to senior Government stakeholders as contract deliverables.
Working knowledge of federal IT oversight frameworks, including FITARA, OMB Circular A-11, and Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) / IT Investment Management (ITIM).
Experience developing performance measures and translating quantitative and qualitative data into decision-ready analysis and recommendations.
Knowledge of enterprise platforms and solutions, such as ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Palantir.
Sound judgment about the boundary between contractor advisory support and Government decision-making, and demonstrated comfort operating within it.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams) and modern collaboration or work management tooling.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to write clearly for a non-technical audience.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver under tight deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications:

Prior experience supporting a federal civilian, foreign affairs, or national security agency.
Experience in environments using commercial SaaS or low-code enterprise platforms hosted in a government cloud – such as ServiceNow, Salesforce, and/or Palantir.
Familiarity with IT cost transparency practices, including cost allocation and consumption-based reporting.
Familiarity with current federal guidance on emerging technology governance.
Experience supporting a newly established office, program management office, or shared service organization.
Agile delivery experience and/or a current certification such as CSM, PSM, PMP, or an ICAgile credential.
Experience building reports and visualizations in Tableau or Power BI.
Familiarity with enterprise architecture practice and reference models.

The salary range for this position is $120,000 - $140,000 and will be commensurate with experience.

Job Description

Are you a compassionate, results-driven professional with the skills necessary to provide assistance within an organization that strives to better the community? If so, WE NEED YOU!

The Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Economic Assistance, is seeking a Child Care Subsidy Fiscal Compliance Analyst to join our team in Lincoln. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys digging into the details, working with financial information, and using facts and sound judgment to reach well-supported conclusions.

Join a team committed to maintaining the integrity of Nebraska’s Child Care Subsidy Program and ensuring public funds are administered responsibly and accurately.

Hiring Rate: $21.855 per hour – Non-Exempt

Work Schedule: Monday – Friday; 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM

Dress Attire: Business Casual

Examples of Work

The Child Care Subsidy Fiscal Compliance Analyst job duties consist of:

Gathering data and requesting information to complete reviews as well as conduct interviews to gather information.
Review claims and determine correct payments to providers.
Use information to compile Excel spreadsheets, Databases; create correspondence, narratives, summaries
Complete detailed reviews of providers and/or clients receiving Child Care Subsidy funds. Prepare report of findings and establish overpayments.
Determination of overpayments for reasons of errors, abuse or misuse of services, contract violations, etc. Determine adjustments to the claims for services.
Prepares reports of findings and establishes case files with supporting documentation/evidence.
Represents the Department at administrative hearings and court proceedings regarding completed reviews.
Be able to apply DHHS rules and regulations and make determinations, using judgment and factual information to determine outcomes.

Requirements/Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
Post high school education or training in bookkeeping, accounting, or mathematics and at least two years of related experience; OR
Bachelor’s degree with emphasis in accounting.

Preferred Qualifications

Any combination of education, training and/or experience with Economic Assistance Programs, accounting or financial practices, report writing, determining overpayments or any similar work.
Previous experience with financial audits, financial investigations or investigative accounting.
Previous experience with claims processing or the Child Care subsidy program.

Other:
Position is located at the Nebraska State Office Building in Lincoln.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Experience with public policy or programs.

Knowledge of:
financial reporting procedures and accounting principles and methods.

Ability to:
calculate addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentage, and decimal computations; perform mathematical operations using fractions, discounts, interest rates, ratios, and proportions; communicate verbally and in writing with other agency staff and client representatives; apply principles of and perform basic level data analysis, and interpret instructions; exercise limited independent judgment and decisiveness in a variety of settings; use a variety of office equipment; handle occasional confrontational individuals within business situations.
